title: Application & Mobile Languages
summary: Java, Kotlin, C#, Swift, Dart and Scala: the languages of enterprise back ends and phone apps. Null safety is the thread running through the modern ones; the UI thread is the threshold of mobile work.
sources: Odersky, Spoon, Venners: Programming in Scala

nodes.label: Java & the JVM
nodes.summary: Bytecode on a virtual machine, garbage collection and a vast ecosystem.
nodes.outcome: Build and run a Java program and explain the JVM's role.
nodes.check: What does 'write once, run anywhere' rely on in Java?
nodes.answer: Compiling to JVM bytecode, which any platform's Java Virtual Machine can run.

nodes.label: Java: Classes & Interfaces
nodes.summary: Single inheritance of classes, multiple interfaces.
nodes.outcome: Design a class hierarchy using interfaces.
nodes.check: What is the difference between an interface and an abstract class in Java?
nodes.answer: A class can implement many interfaces but extend only one class; interfaces define a contract, abstract classes can also hold state and shared code.

nodes.label: "Java passes objects by reference"
nodes.summary: Java is always pass-by-value; for objects, the value passed is a copy of the reference.
nodes.outcome: Predict whether a method can replace a caller's object.
nodes.check: Does Java pass object arguments by reference?
nodes.answer: No: Java is always pass-by-value; for objects, the value passed is a copy of the reference.

nodes.label: Kotlin: Null Safety
nodes.summary: Nullable types are explicit, and the compiler forces checks.
nodes.outcome: Use safe calls and the Elvis operator.
nodes.check: In Kotlin, can a variable of type String (without a question mark) hold null?
nodes.answer: No: only the nullable type String? can, and the compiler forces null checks.

nodes.label: C# & .NET
nodes.summary: A statically typed language for Windows, web, games (Unity) and cloud.
nodes.check: What does LINQ let you do in C#?
nodes.answer: Query collections, databases and XML with a uniform, SQL-like syntax inside the language.

nodes.label: Swift: Optionals & iOS
nodes.summary: Value types, optionals and SwiftUI for Apple platforms.
nodes.check: What does Swift's 'if let' do with an optional?
nodes.answer: Unwraps it safely: the block runs only if the optional holds a value.

nodes.label: Dart & Flutter
nodes.summary: One codebase for Android, iOS, web and desktop.
nodes.outcome: Build a Flutter screen and use hot reload.
nodes.check: What does Flutter's hot reload do?
nodes.answer: It injects changed code into the running app so the UI updates in about a second without losing state.

nodes.label: Scala: Functional on the JVM
nodes.summary: Object-oriented and functional, with a powerful type system.
nodes.outcome: Write a data pipeline with Scala collections.
nodes.check: Which big-data engine is written in Scala?

nodes.label: Mobile App Architecture
nodes.summary: The UI thread must never block; lifecycles, background work and offline state shape every design.
nodes.outcome: Move slow work off the UI thread and survive app lifecycle changes.
nodes.check: Why must long network calls stay off a mobile app's main (UI) thread?
nodes.answer: The UI would freeze, and the operating system may kill an unresponsive app.

nodes.label: "Cross-platform means no native code, ever"
nodes.summary: Platform features without a plugin still need Swift or Kotlin through platform channels or native modules.
nodes.outcome: Plan where native code is needed in a cross-platform app.
nodes.check: Does a Flutter or React Native app ever need native Swift or Kotlin code?
nodes.answer: Sometimes: platform features without a plugin need native code through platform channels or native modules.
